criteria.criterion: Gate regression test: a commit that adds an athena.toml section and the matching athena-data schema change in one commit produces no Configuration violation from athena-gate content::check, while the same athena.toml change without a schema change is still refused with the parse error. Run: cargo test -p athena-gate.
criteria.evidence: content::tests::a_new_section_with_its_schema_change_in_one_commit_is_not_refused passed. It first asserts the running schema rejects [parallel], then shows no Rule::Configuration violation when the same commit also touches crates/athena-data/src/lib.rs, and shows an 'unknown field' Configuration violation when only athena.toml changes. deleting_the_schema_does_not_defer_the_parse also passed. The full suite passed too.

criteria.criterion: Admission test: a candidate changing both crates/athena-data/ and athena.toml is admitted without any process being spawned to build candidate code, and an unknown section with no schema change is still a violation. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: a_new_section_and_its_schema_change_together_are_admitted_without_a_build and an_unknown_section_without_a_schema_change_is_still_refused both passed. The test repo has no Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock, so any build attempt would fail and show up as a violation. The code path for a schema change is now just `None`, and admission.rs has no process spawn left.

criteria.criterion: admission.rs no longer contains check_with_candidate_schema, CHECK_MAIN, or any Command::new(cargo) use on candidate files; grep shows none in athena-core or athena-gate.
criteria.evidence: A Grep over crates/athena-core and crates/athena-gate finds no check_with_candidate_schema or CHECK_MAIN. The remaining Command::new calls are git (pin.rs, introspect.rs), gh/curl (gh.rs), the configured check runner (checks.rs) and gitleaks (secrets.rs). None of them runs cargo on candidate files.

criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-data parses the repository's athena.toml and defaults.toml with that crate's own schema and fails if either does not parse, so a candidate's sandboxed cargo test judges its own schema. Run: cargo test -p athena-data.
criteria.evidence: The new tests/repo_config.rs reads ../../athena.toml and ../../defaults.toml relative to CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR and panics if Config::parse or DefaultsModel::parse fails. All 3 tests passed, including one showing an unknown section fails to parse.

criteria.criterion: Both checks use one shared rule for deciding when to defer to the sandboxed test, so gate and admission cannot diverge. Run: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt --check all pass.
criteria.evidence: athena_gate::defers_to_schema_test in lib.rs is called by both content.rs check and admission.rs admit_without_secrets. fmt and clippy passed. The full test run passed with no failures, which I read in the cargo test -q output.

criteria.criterion: A short design note records the decision with alternatives (host build, sandbox build, lenient parse) and states why candidate code is never built on the host; CHANGELOG notes the change.
criteria.evidence: docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md gains a section 'Judging configuration by the candidate's schema' that gives the decision, three rejected alternatives (host build, isolated build, lenient parse) and the reason: the candidate's author controls what the build runs. CHANGELOG has a new Changed entry naming the root cause, the shared rule and the tests.

findings.summary: When the parse is deferred, the [history] exempt ancestor check can be skipped silently
findings.evidence: new_exemptions returns no violations when Config::parse(text) fails with the running schema. Before this change such a parse failure was also a Configuration violation. Now a commit that touches crates/athena-data/ and adds both an unknown section and a new exempt entry gets neither check at landing. The athena.toml governance rule still applies, which limits the risk.

findings.summary: The admission test proves 'no build' indirectly
findings.evidence: The test does not observe directly that no process is spawned. It relies on the fixture lacking Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, so a build would fail. Since the build code is removed, this is adequate.

findings.summary: Awkward rewrite of the earlier CHANGELOG entry
findings.evidence: The earlier entry now begins 'Admission judges (superseded by the entry above: the host build was removed) a changed ...'. The parenthetical splits the sentence.

summary: The change fixes both checks at the root, as the request asked. A new function, athena_gate::defers_to_schema_test, decides for both the landing gate and admission when a commit changes crates/athena-data/; in that case neither check parses athena.toml or defaults.toml itself. They leave the file to a new test in the candidate's own athena-data (tests/repo_config.rs), which runs in the candidate's sandboxed cargo test. The host-side builder in admission (check_with_candidate_schema, CHECK_MAIN, the cargo run) is removed, so candidate code is never built on the host. I ran the gate, admission and athena-data tests, cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets and the full cargo test; all passed. The new tests show three things: a section added with its schema change is not refused, the same section without a schema change is still refused with the parse error, and the repository's config files parse with the crate's own schema. The design note and CHANGELOG are present. Every changed file is on the deliverables list; Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock were listed but did not need to change. Findings: one minor (the [history] exempt ancestor check can be skipped silently when the parse is deferred), one minor (the admission test proves "no build" only indirectly) and one nit (the CHANGELOG wording).
